This post is from the blog I kept as Preceptor in Mathematics at Harvard (2005–2008). It's kept here as an archive; some links are dead and references are dated.
:::

I just found [PhpMathPublisher](http://www.xm1math.net/phpmathpublisher/) on the web and it looks kind of interesting. The name pretty much describes it: a PHP package that parses a kind of math input and produces image-based output.

Most packages (such as [LaTeXRender](http://www.mayer.dial.pipex.com/tex.htm)) along these lines serve as a front end to TeX or LaTeX, then serve up a generated image file. There are some drawbacks to this:

- TeX and LaTeX are complicated programs with huge distributions, and may not be available to all web programmers
- because these programs can include files, there’s a potential security leak in allowing all web users to effectively execute TeX code on the server.

PhpMathPublisher has a tex-like syntax but seems to parse the input on its own and use GD to assemble a formula. Here’s the markup:

\
`<m>delim{|}{{1/N} sum{n=1}{N}{gamma(u_n)} - 1/{2 pi} int{0}{2 pi}{gamma(t) dt}}{|} <= epsilon/3</m>`\

[![](http://www.xm1math.net/phpmathpublisher/doc/sample.png){border="0"}](http://www.xm1math.net/phpmathpublisher/)

In LaTeX we would write

`\left|\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^n \gamma(u_n) - \frac{1}{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi} \gamma(t)\,dt\right| \leq \frac{\varepsilon}{3}`

to get

![\\displaystyle\\left\|\\frac{1}{N}\\sum\_{n=1}\^n \\gamma(u_n) - \\frac{1}{2\\pi}\\int_0\^{2\\pi} \\gamma(t)\\,dt\\right\| \\leq \\frac{\\varepsilon}{3}](/images/be500655d5eefe2613c35b20b123d4dd.png "\displaystyle\left|\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^n \gamma(u_n) - \frac{1}{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi} \gamma(t)\,dt\right| \leq \frac{\varepsilon}{3}"){align="absmiddle"}

It does get the job done, and the finished product is not so bad.
